key_insight: M3-Score breaks generative radiology evaluation into three separate axes—fidelity, memorization, and coverage—so models can be judged for image realism and diversity instead of by one blended score.
clinical_relevance: A more radiology-aware evaluation metric may better detect whether synthetic medical images preserve clinically important structures without simply copying training data or missing rare findings.
method: Uses a frozen radiology-pretrained vision transformer (RadioDINO-s16) as the feature encoder.
Computes fidelity with unbiased multi-bandwidth RBF MMD^2 at the final block.
Measures memorization with nearest-neighbor distances and coverage with k-NN radius overlap at earlier encoder depths.
evidence_signal: In BraTS MRI experiments, the fidelity axis ranked five increasingly severe comparison sets perfectly (Spearman ρ=1.00), the subject-disjoint real set gave MMD^2=0, and the coverage axis tracked progressive mode dropping monotonically (ρ=-1.00).
watch_item: Results depend on a specific radiology-pretrained encoder and subject-level sampling design, so generalization to other modalities, scanners, or datasets may require revalidation.
paper_title: M3-Score: Fidelity, Memorization and Coverage as Separate Axes for Evaluating Generative Radiology Image Models
